1.s: Paul thanks God for the Corinthians but rebukes their divisions: “I follow Paul,” “I follow Apollos.” The message of the cross is foolishness to the world, but God’s power.
1.d: Some in Corinth prized eloquence and human wisdom; Paul sets against them the plain message of the cross, which shows God’s wisdom [[tosn:1 Corinthians 1:18-31]]. “We preach Christ crucified” [[bible:1 Corinthians 1:23]]: many Jews thought a crucified Messiah a contradiction, since crucifixion seemed to show God’s curse (Deuteronomy 21:23) [[tosn:1 Corinthians 1:23]].

2.s: Paul came not with clever speech but in weakness, so faith would rest on God’s power. The Spirit reveals God’s wisdom.
2.d: Paul did not try to sound clever; he taught them about Jesus’ death on the cross [[bsn:1 Corinthians 2:1-16]]. God has given his Spirit to his people so that they can know what he has freely given them [[tosn:1 Corinthians 2:10-12]].

3.s: The church is God’s field and God’s building; Paul planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth. “You are a temple of God.”
3.d: The church’s only foundation is Jesus Christ himself [[tosn:1 Corinthians 3:11]]. On judgment day the work of each teacher who builds on it will be tested [[tosn:1 Corinthians 3:12-15]], and teaching about Jesus that is not true will burn [[bsn:1 Corinthians 3:10-23]].

4.s: Apostles are servants and stewards; Paul describes their hardships and calls the Corinthians to imitate him.
4.d: “What do you have that you didn’t receive?” [[bible:1 Corinthians 4:7]] Pride in a leader comes from forgetting that everything is a gift from God [[tosn:1 Corinthians 4:7]].

5.s: A man living with his father’s wife must be removed from the church. A little yeast leavens the whole lump.
5.d: Before Passover, Jews removed yeast from their homes [[tosn:1 Corinthians 5:6-7]]. Christ’s sacrifice happened at Passover, and Paul calls him our Passover Lamb [[tosn:1 Corinthians 5:7-8]] [[bsn:1 Corinthians 5:1-13]].

6.s: Believers should not take each other to court. Sexual immorality is a sin against the body: “Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit.” “You were bought with a price.”
6.d: Some in Corinth argued that the body was made for sex; Paul answers that our bodies were made for the Lord [[tosn:1 Corinthians 6:13-14]]. God raised Jesus’ body from the dead, and the Holy Spirit lives in each believer’s body [[bsn:1 Corinthians 6:12-20]] [[tosn:1 Corinthians 6:18-20]].

7.s: Paul answers questions on marriage, singleness and divorce, valuing both marriage and singleness as gifts.
7.d: “Not I, but the Lord” does not make Paul’s other advice less authoritative: here he passes on Jesus’ own known teaching on divorce (Matthew 5:32; Mark 10:11–12) [[tosn:1 Corinthians 7:10-11]]. Where Jesus gave no specific word, Paul still speaks clearly [[tosn:1 Corinthians 7:12-13]].

8.s: On food offered to idols: knowledge puffs up, but love builds up. Don’t let your freedom make a weaker believer stumble.
8.d: Paul confesses one God, the Father, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things were created (compare John 1:3; Colossians 1:16) [[tosn:1 Corinthians 8:4-6]].

9.s: Paul gives up his rights for the sake of the gospel: “I have become all things to all men, that I may by all means save some.”
9.d: Athletes train with strict self-discipline to win a prize; Christians need the same discipline for the prize that lasts for ever [[tosn:1 Corinthians 9:24-27]].

10.s: Israel’s wilderness story is a warning. “God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able.” Do everything for God’s glory.
10.d: “The rock was Christ” refers to the rock Moses struck for water (Exodus 17:1–7; Numbers 20). Early Jewish tradition held that both miracles involved the same travelling rock, and Paul reads Israel’s wilderness provision alongside the Lord’s Supper [[tosn:1 Corinthians 10:3-4]].

11.s: Head coverings in worship, and abuses at the Lord’s Supper. Paul repeats the tradition: “This is my body… this cup is the new covenant in my blood.”
11.d: “I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you” [[bible:1 Corinthians 11:23]]: one of the few clear places where Paul passes on a tradition coming from Christ [[tosn:1 Corinthians 11:23]]. The letter was written around AD 53–56 [[tosn:1 Corinthians 15:6]], from Ephesus [[tbd:006:First Letter to the Corinthians]].

12.s: Spiritual gifts: one Spirit, many gifts. The church is one body with many parts; each needs the others.
12.d: The church is one body with many parts, each placed where God wants it [[tosn:1 Corinthians 12:14-21]]; the weaker, less noticed parts are needed and deserve special care [[tosn:1 Corinthians 12:22-26]].

13.s: “If I speak with the languages of men and of angels, but don’t have love…” “Love is patient and is kind… love never fails.” “Now faith, hope, and love remain… The greatest of these is love.”
13.d: The Corinthians made too much of speaking in tongues [[tosn:1 Corinthians 12:1-14:40]]. Paul pauses his teaching on spiritual gifts to show that love is greater than any gift [[tosn:1 Corinthians 13:1-13]], and that love, unlike the gifts, lasts for ever [[tosn:1 Corinthians 13:8-13]].

14.s: Prophecy builds up the church more than tongues. Worship should be orderly and understandable.
14.d: “God is not a God of confusion, but of peace” [[bible:1 Corinthians 14:33]]: worship should reflect a God of peace and order [[bsn:1 Corinthians 14:26-40]].

15.s: Christ died for our sins, was buried, was raised on the third day, and appeared to Peter, the Twelve, five hundred, James and Paul. If Christ is not raised, faith is in vain. The resurrection body. “Death, where is your sting?”
15.d: Paul passes on what he “received”: Christ died for our sins, was buried, was raised on the third day, and appeared to many [[bible:1 Corinthians 15:3-8]]; this is the tradition of Christian teaching shared by word of mouth [[tosn:1 Corinthians 11:2]]. Most of the more than five hundred witnesses were still alive, so readers could ask them [[tosn:1 Corinthians 15:6]].

16.s: A collection for the poor in Jerusalem, travel plans and greetings. Paul’s closing prayer: “Come, Lord!”
16.d: Paul adds a greeting in his own hand, as he did in other letters [[tosn:1 Corinthians 16:21]]. “Come, Lord!” was a prayer early Christians used (compare Revelation 22:20) [[tosn:1 Corinthians 16:22]]. The collection was for needy Jewish believers in Jerusalem [[bsn:1 Corinthians 16:1-24]].
